Section 3 One Single BLSTM network for WSD states that the architecture, depicted in Fig. 1, consists of 6 layers. The layer count is explicit: 6 layers. This total answers the question of how many layers the model has.

The named layers that make up the architecture are a sigmoid layer (at the top), a fully-connected layer, a concatenation layer, a BLSTM layer, a cosine layer, and a sense and word embeddings layer. The paper includes the sense and word embeddings layer as one of the six layers, on the bottom. The BLSTM is treated as one layer within the total layer count; the paper lists the BLSTM layer as one of the six layers. The model therefore uses a single BLSTM layer as a component within the 6 layers.

No other explicit total layer count for the model is stated in the paper. The explicit total layer count given is 6 layers. The named components define the full layer structure: sigmoid, fully-connected, concatenation, BLSTM, cosine, and sense and word embeddings. The sense and word embeddings layer sits on the bottom, and the sigmoid layer sits at the top. These facts answer the architecture-layer and layer-count queries for the single classifier bidirectional LSTM WSD model.
